lesson_scope: Right-angled triangle properties, trigonometric angle determination in radians, sector areas inside right triangles, region outside sector inside triangle, internal projection triangles, and complementary vertex sectors.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct trigonometric ratio and right triangle area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of tan(A) = opp/adj and Area = 0.5*base*height.

hints: In right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, $\tan(\angle A) = \dfrac{BC}{AC}$.
Substitute $BC = 6$ and $AC = 8$ to find $\tan(\angle A) = \dfrac{6}{8} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.
Calculate the area using $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC = \dfrac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the opposite and adjacent legs to angle $\angle A$ in right triangle $\triangle ABC$:
$$\tan(\angle A) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{BC}{AC} = \frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24\text{ cm}^2$$

walkthrough.text:
State the sector area formula for radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$ and central angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$:

Substitute the values and simplify:

hints: Find the area of the right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$: $\dfrac{1}{2}(4)(4\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.
Find the area of the sector of radius $4\text{ cm}$ and angle $\pi/3$: $\dfrac{1}{2}(4^2)(\pi/3) = \dfrac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$.
Subtract the sector area from the triangle area: $8\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{8\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC = \frac{1}{2}(4)(4\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the sector centred at $A$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the total triangle area to get the remaining region:
$$A = 8\sqrt{3} - \frac{8\pi}{3} = \left(8\sqrt{3} - \frac{8\pi}{3}\right)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates triangle area $8\sqrt{3}$ and sector area $\dfrac{8\pi}{3}$.
Subtracts sector from triangle to obtain $\left(8\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{8\pi}{3}\right)\text{ cm}^2$.

hints: In right triangle $\triangle OPB$, hypotenuse $OB = r = 10\text{ cm}$ and vertex angle $\angle POB = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
The legs are $OP = 10\cos(\pi/6) = 5\sqrt{3}$ and $PB = 10\sin(\pi/6) = 5$.
Calculate area: $\dfrac{1}{2}(OP)(PB) = \dfrac{1}{2}(5\sqrt{3})(5) = \dfrac{25\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text: In right-angled triangle $\triangle OPB$, hypotenuse is the radius $OB = 10\text{ cm}$ and angle $\angle POB = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the lengths of the two perpendicular legs:
$$OP = 10\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$$
$$PB = 10\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = 10 \times \frac{1}{2} = 5\text{ cm}$$

Compute the area of the right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OPB) = \frac{1}{2} \times OP \times PB = \frac{1}{2}(5\sqrt{3})(5) = \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2$$

hints: The two acute angles in a right-angled triangle sum to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$: $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
The sum of the two sector areas is $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\alpha + \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\alpha + \beta)$.
Substitute $r = 4$ and $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$: $\dfrac{1}{2}(16)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 4\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
In any right-angled triangle, the sum of the two acute angles is:
$$\alpha + \beta = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$$

Express the total area of the two sectors of equal radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Total Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\alpha + \frac{1}{2}r^2\beta = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\alpha + \beta)$$

Substitute $r = 4$ and $\alpha + \beta = \frac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\text{Total Area} = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 8 \times \frac{\pi}{2} = 4\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains exact total sector area $4\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of boundary tracing P = leg + remainder + arc.

hints: Find the hypotenuse: $AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10\text{ cm}$.
The remainder segment on the hypotenuse is $EB = AB - AE = 10 - 6 = 4\text{ cm}$.
Find the arc length: $s = r\theta = 6(0.927) = 5.562\text{ cm}$, and sum $BC + EB + s = 8 + 4 + 5.562 = 17.562\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the length of hypotenuse $AB$ by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\text{ cm}$$

Subtract the radius $AE = 6\text{ cm}$ to find the straight segment $EB$:
$$EB = AB - AE = 10 - 6 = 4\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the arc length $CE$:
$$s = r\theta = 6 \times 0.927 = 5.562\text{ cm}$$

Sum the three boundary components:
$$P = BC + EB + s = 8 + 4 + 5.562 = 17.562\text{ cm}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $P = 17.6\text{ cm}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains perimeter $8 + 4 + 5.562 = 17.562\dots$ and rounds to $17.6\text{ cm}$ (3 s.f.).

hints: In a right triangle with hypotenuse $13$ and leg $5$, the vertex opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ leg has adjacent side $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}$.

The acute angle satisfies $\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}$ or $\cos\theta = \dfrac{12}{13}$, so $\theta = \cos^{-1}(12/13) \approx 0.3948\text{ rad}$ or $\cos^{-1}(5/13) = 1.176\text{ rad}$ depending on vertex orientation.

walkthrough.text:
Find the acute angle at the vertex opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ leg:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{5}{13} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 1.176005\text{ radians}$$
Rounding to $3$ decimal places gives $\theta = 1.176\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the area of the sector of radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)(1.176005) = 18(1.176005) = 21.1681\text{ cm}^2$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $A = 21.2\text{ cm}^2$.

hints: The sector area is $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.
The right triangle has hypotenuse $r$, adjacent leg $r\cos\theta$, and opposite leg $r\sin\theta$, so its area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(r\cos\theta)(r\sin\theta) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta$.
Factor out $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2$ from the difference, and state the domain $0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ required for the right triangle to remain inside the sector.

walkthrough.text: In the internal right triangle, the hypotenuse is the circle radius $r$ and the acute angle at the centre is $\theta$.

The lengths of the adjacent and opposite legs are:
$$\text{base} = r\cos\theta, \quad \text{height} = r\sin\theta$$
$$\text{Area}(\triangle) = \frac{1}{2}(r\cos\theta)(r\sin\theta) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$
The area of the sector is $\text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area and factorise:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta - \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta\cos\theta)$$
For the right triangle to exist with an acute angle $\theta$ and lie strictly within a quadrant, the central angle must satisfy $0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies triangle hypotenuse $r$ and legs $r\cos\theta$ and $r\sin\theta$.
Notes requirement $\theta < \pi/2$ for internal right triangle.

hints: The vertex opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ leg has acute angle $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(5/12)$. Sector area with $r = 12$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}(12^2)\alpha = 72\alpha$.
The other acute vertex has complementary angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \alpha$. Sector area with $r = 5$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}(5^2)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \dfrac{25\pi}{4} - \dfrac{25}{2}\alpha$.

Sum the two sector areas: $72\alpha + \dfrac{25\pi}{4} - \dfrac{25}{2}\alpha = \dfrac{25\pi}{4} + \dfrac{119}{2}\alpha$, then evaluate to $3$ significant figures using $\alpha \approx 0.394791\text{ radians}$.

walkthrough.text: In the right triangle with legs $12\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$, the acute angle opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ leg is $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)$.

Calculate the area of the first sector (centred at that vertex with radius $r_1 = 12\text{ cm}$):
$$A_1 = \frac{1}{2}r_1^2\alpha = \frac{1}{2}(12^2)\alpha = 72\alpha\text{ cm}^2$$

The angle at the other acute vertex is the complement $\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha$. Calculate the area of the second sector (radius $r_2 = 5\text{ cm}$):
$$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}r_2^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \frac{25\pi}{4} - \frac{25}{2}\alpha\text{ cm}^2$$

Add the two sector areas to find the exact sum in terms of $\alpha$:
$$A_{\text{total}} = 72\alpha + \frac{25\pi}{4} - \frac{25}{2}\alpha = \frac{25\pi}{4} + \left(72 - \frac{25}{2}\right)\alpha = \left(\frac{25\pi}{4} + \frac{119}{2}\alpha\right)\text{ cm}^2$$

Evaluate using $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right) \approx 0.394791\text{ radians}$:
$$A_{\text{total}} = \frac{25\pi}{4} + 59.5(0.394791) \approx 19.6350 + 23.4901 = 51.5251\text{ cm}^2$$
(With exact triangle area $30\text{ cm}^2$, rounding gives $51.5\text{ cm}^2$).

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the two acute angles as $\alpha$ and $\pi/2 - \alpha$.
Obtains $51.524\dots$ and rounds to $51.5\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).
